machine: WSL2 i5-14400 host, 16 logical CPUs, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (driver 13030) — same host as gpu-sidecar.bench.json
purpose: ticket 04 runtime input: laya-rust (candle) vs laya-goish CPU engine vs GPU sidecar, same weights, same inputs

build_cuda.result: PASS after environment work (initially: cudarc v0.19.9 build-script exit 101 — bare `nvcc --version` not found, 13.4 not in supported list)
build_cuda.recipe_summary: pip wheels pinned 13.3.x (nvcc/nvvm/crt/cccl/runtime/cublas/curand/nvrtc), CUDA_HOME symlink farm with unversioned dev .so names + libcuda.so from /usr/lib/wsl/lib, CUDARC_CUDA_VERSION=13030 (env beats build-system detection), CUDA_PATH also required (bindgen_cuda ignores CUDA_HOME), LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64 at runtime
build_cuda.ptx_versions: nvcc 13.4 wheels emit PTX .version 9.4 (toolchain-driven; CUDA_COMPUTE_CAP does not change it) -> driver 13030 rejects; all-13.3 wheels emit .version 9.3/.target sm_120 -> loads and runs
build_cuda.runtime_dtype: f32 works; f16 on CUDA produces NaN logits and panics in laya-rust src/model.rs:232 (partial_cmp on NaN)

weight_equivalence.evidence: refund noul, identical 45-token state: laya-rust 0.8911 (4 dp print) vs laya-goish 0.8911915421 (= committed examples/refund.output.json 0.8911915421485901)
weight_equivalence.trailing_newline_variant: CLI --state-file with trailing newline -> 46 tokens -> noul 0.8902

warm_latency_ms.protocol: laya-rust: in-process loop, 3 warmups, n=30, includes tokenization; laya-goish CPU: usage.latency_ms from ./laya decide --raw --threads 16, n=3; GPU: sidecar socket round trip, token IDs in, 1 warmup

urgent_2q.note: laya-rust: one batched 124-token pass for both questions; laya-goish: per-question prompts 68 + 81 tokens, two passes

laya_rust_cuda_vs_gpu_sidecar.refund: 18.7 vs 33.4 ms — cuBLAS 1.8x faster than sidecar scalar-FMA matmul
laya_rust_cuda_vs_gpu_sidecar.urgent: 27.6 vs 110.3 ms — 4x via one batched 124-token pass vs two sequential passes
laya_rust_cuda_vs_gpu_sidecar.verification: nvidia-smi during bench: 4473 MiB in use; answers identical to laya-rust CPU (refund noul 0.8911)

answers_urgent_case.finding: choice flip route billing vs technical from prompt composition (batched multi-question vs per-question), same weights; urgency stays close

decision: Not adopted as the engine for ticket 04, but its matmul path is: link pip-wheel libcublas.so.13 in the sidecar (proven viable here) or move matmul to tensor cores, and consider batched multi-question prompts (27.6 vs 110.3 ms on urgent). laya-rust itself remains unsuitable as a drop-in: no GGUF graph_spec, no OpenThai, batched prompts flip route on urgent, f16-on-CUDA NaNs in its own code, f32 residency 1.7 GB/model does not fit the two-model budget. See laya-rust-comparison.report.md.

appendix.gpu_urgent_bench_protocol: sidecar serve; for each question from validation/gpu-drift.py cpu_decide(): sidecar_request({ids, markers, qtype}) x10 after warmup; per-question and paired-total timings above
